clue.text: Hang fish on front of door

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another goes after it
front of picks out the opening letter of the word door

parts.note: to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: An instruction to hang a fish on the front door, perhaps as a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the fish after D, the first letter of 'door'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms as verbs: to dangle is to hang loosely or suspend.

clue.text: Humourless, stifling anything breezy

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: dry can describe humour, but also dull and humourless
aught is an old word for anything

explanation.surface: A dour person suppressing anything lighthearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breezy' sounds like a cheerful manner but here means windy; 'aught' is an old word for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a room with cold air blowing through it is breezy.

clue.text: Author hopelessly in love with good man

indicators.note: hopelessly signals the letters of in love are thrown into disorder

parts.note: ST, saint, is a crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: A writer besotted with a virtuous man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hopelessly' turns IN LOVE into NOVELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of fiction books is a kind of author.

clue.text: More available, perhaps, for corrective punishment

definitions.text: More available, perhaps, for corrective punishment

parts.words: More available, perhaps, for corrective punishment
parts.note: split into two words, the answer suggests a smaller quantity on offer, the opposite of more available; 'perhaps' flags the quirky reading

explanation.walkthrough: The answer split as two words means fewer things on offer, the reverse of 'More available'; 'perhaps' warns of the loose fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment that teaches the offender to behave better is a salutary lecture of this kind.

clue.text: Gold medallist is back

definitions.meaning: a gold medallist is the winner of an event
to back a cause is to support or stand up for it

explanation.surface: An athlete who won gold is returning to competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner of first place is the title-holder; as a verb, to support a cause is to champion it.

clue.text: British ultimately having to suffer cold weather

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the closing letter of the word British

parts.note: to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: The British are destined to put up with chilly weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen rain falling as ice pellets is a form of cold weather.

clue.text: How intelligent I am to keep way above upper echelons, initially — powerful aura!

indicators.note: in a down clue, above places this piece before the next one
to keep is to hold, so one piece contains another

parts.note: the measure of my intelligence is my IQ
ST, street, is a way

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of upper and echelons

explanation.surface: A boast about one's own intellect keeping one at the top, creating an air of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How intelligent I am' is a phrase to be turned into a measure: my intelligence quotient.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystique is an aura of mystery or power surrounding a person.

clue.text: Is king upstate?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading from the bottom upwards, and the state then names what the whole clue describes

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A question about whether a monarch lives in the north of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: Lear is Shakespeare's king; 'upstate' both turns him upwards and hints that the whole clue describes a state.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a Middle Eastern country, an example of a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Relative seeing topless individual, I'm perspiring!

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is taken off, the top in a down clue

parts.note: one is a single individual
phew is the exclamation of someone hot and sweaty

explanation.surface: Someone sweating with embarrassment after seeing a relative with no top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' takes the O off ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Guide I saved after a mauling

indicators.note: something that has been mauled is torn about, so the letters of I saved are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has rescued another from an animal attack and now guides them.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to guide someone is to counsel them on what to do.

clue.text: Land here shows journey

parts.note: to show something on television is to air it, so shows gives airs
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: A sign announcing that the land beneath displays a voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway strip is a place where a light aircraft can touch down.

clue.text: Supreme power corrupting James ends in absolutist monarchy

indicators.note: corrupting means spoiling, so the letters of James are distorted
ends in picks the last letters of absolutist and monarchy

explanation.surface: King James corrupted by absolute monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupting' turns JAMES into MAJES.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is sovereign power and the dignity of a monarch.

clue.text: Scottish region happy to claim grant

indicators.note: to claim something is to take it in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: gay in its older sense means merry or happy
to grant a request is to allow it

explanation.surface: A Scottish area that is pleased to apply for public funding.
explanation.walkthrough: Galloway is an area of south-west Scotland; 'happy' uses the older sense of gay, merry.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: Galloway is a historic area in the south-west of Scotland.

clue.text: How paper may be sold, did you say, in old vessel?

indicators.note: a spoken question asking if we heard rightly, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: paper is sold by the ream, a bundle of 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A question about selling paper aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A ream is a standard bundle of paper sheets; 'by ream' spoken resembles the ship's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A bireme was an ancient galley with two banks of oars, so an old vessel.

clue.text: One for the road, particularly in restaurant

parts.note: a car is a vehicle for the road, not the usual drink
very means particularly

explanation.surface: A final drink, especially in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One for the road' looks like a last drink but is a vehicle. A carvery is a British restaurant serving roast meat carved to order.
explanation.definitionFit: A carvery is an eatery where roast joints are sliced for diners, a type of restaurant.

clue.text: American behind an expression of disgust

definitions.meaning: in US slang a person's bottom
an old exclamation of impatience or contempt, like pish

explanation.surface: An American trailing behind a cry of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: US slang for buttocks, and an archaic interjection of scorn or impatience.

clue.text: Stomach about full, ultimately, with American nation

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to stomach something is to bear or tolerate it

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the closing letter of the word full

parts.note: US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: A full stomach after an American meal, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like a noun but is the verb, BEAR; 'about' puts L (the end of 'full') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Belarus is an Eastern European country, an example of a nation.

clue.text: Obligatory papers marked urgent, it's suggested?

indicators.note: papers marked in red ink sit within the red, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: red is the colour of urgency and alarm
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Documents labelled urgent, so it is said, are compulsory.
explanation.walkthrough: A quire is a paper measure of about two dozen sheets; 'it's suggested' admits the looseness of red for urgent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something compulsory is demanded by rule.

clue.text: Hungry Mennonites provided with bags

indicators.note: to bag is to capture or enclose, so one piece holds another

parts.note: fed means provided with food
the Amish are a Mennonite community

explanation.surface: Hungry Mennonites are given bags of food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' is a verb: FED holds AMISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to be starving is to be extremely hungry.

clue.text: Trap good, rely on moving with caution

parts.note: a gin is a snare for catching animals

indicators.note: moving means shifting about, so the letters of rely are rearranged

explanation.surface: Relying on a good trap as one moves cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' turns RELY into ERLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb synonyms: doing something carefully, tentatively, with great care.

clue.text: Jolly unusual set among with-it children, literally?

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: E. Nesbit's novel Five Children and It: the children who are with It number five

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of set are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Fashionable kids are a cheerful, unusual group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with-it' looks like 'trendy' but is read literally: the children with It in Nesbit's book. 'unusual' turns SET into EST, which goes 'among' FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a cheerful, celebratory mood, as at a party or holiday.

clue.text: Queen ruled over India for a start

parts.note: to run a country is to rule over it, so ran

indicators.note: for a start picks the opening letter of the word India

explanation.surface: A queen who governed India in its early days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruled over' looks like the reign of the queen, but just gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A rani is a Hindu queen or a raja's wife, so a royal consort or monarch.

clue.text: Man is breaking most of biscuit for primate

indicators.note: breaking means going into, so one piece splits the other
most of says the final letter is removed

parts.note: a rusk is a hard dry biscuit
he is the pronoun for a man
is shortens to 's

explanation.surface: A man breaking a biscuit for a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims RUSK to RUS, and 'breaking' puts HES inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus macaque is a monkey, a kind of primate.

clue.text: Badger baiting primarily remaining

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the word baiting

parts.note: the other ones are the remaining ones

explanation.surface: Badger-baiting still persists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' looks like the animal but is the verb, to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to badger someone is to pester or annoy them.

clue.text: Sweet thing in extraterrestrial, certainly uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something sweet found in an alien, which is certainly cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifting' reads the letters bottom to top; no word signals the concealment, so 'in' is doing that job.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate is a sweet treat.

clue.text: Meet westbound bear touring Britain

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading from right to left
touring means travelling round, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: Pooh is the famous bear of A. A. Milne's stories
UK is the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: A bear on a tour of Britain heading west to meet someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' is Winnie-the-Pooh; 'Meet' is a noun here, a get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, a meeting or link-up is a connection between parties; meet here is a noun, a gathering.

clue.text: Wonderful failing

definitions.meaning: giving way or breaking under strain

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: British slang for excellent, and splitting or breaking down under pressure.

clue.text: European conclusions of Chief Rabbi in question

indicators.note: conclusions of picks the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A European is the subject of the Chief Rabbi's inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland, a Nordic country, is a European.

clue.text: Solid favourite relishes making a comeback on the outside

parts.note: dips are savoury sauces or relishes
a hero is a favourite, an idol

explanation.surface: A firm favourite enjoys a return to form outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a comeback' turns DIPS into SPID, which goes 'on the outside' of HERO.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a solid is a three-dimensional figure; a ball-like one is an example.

clue.text: Baptist ring

definitions.meaning: one who baptises, washing people in water
a flat ring placed under a nut or bolt

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one who cleans by immersion, as at a baptism, and a flat disc used in plumbing or engineering.

clue.text: Loud weapon behind bow of ship

indicators.note: behind says this piece comes after the next one
the bow is the front of a ship, so bow of picks the first letter of the word ship

parts.note: a trident is a three-pronged spear

explanation.surface: A noisy weapon mounted behind a ship's bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' puts TRIDENT after S, the first letter of 'ship'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: harsh and piercing in sound, like a loud voice or trumpet.

clue.text: One of seven, free in spirit

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a fay is a fairy, a spirit
to rid is to free

explanation.surface: One of seven people is a free spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of seven' is a day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: The week has seven days, and this weekday is one of them.
